F01.statement: Czajkowski, Coulais, van Hecke and Rocklin; Nature Communications 13, 211; published 11 January 2022; DOI suffix contains 2021 but publication year is 2022.

F02.statement: Printed meta-beam: 306 mm length, 64 mm width, 40 mm height; 48 by 10 squares; square side 4.8 mm; hinge thickness 0.2 mm.

F03.statement: Connex 500 Stratasys fabrication using proprietary Agilus 30, nominal 30 Shore A; Vero Black square pads of 3.6 mm were printed on one edge for imaging.

F04.statement: The material is viscoelastic. Referenced short/long-time Young moduli are 3.3 MPa and 0.6 MPa; these are cited values rather than a new specimen calibration trace supplied here.

F05.statement: Physical branch 1 uses a foot-shaped ABS indenter printed on a Stratasys Dimension printer. Fine powder lubricates contact with the bottom surface and foot; powder identity and amount are not specified.

F06.statement: Foot branch: a compression-decompression cycle at 0.1 mm/s to maximum 20 mm stroke, recording 400 frames at 1 frame/s.

F07.statement: Physical branch 2 is a three-point bridge loading test using an Instron 5943; a compression-decompression cycle at 0.2 mm/s to maximum 40 mm stroke, recording 400 frames at 1 frame/s.

F08.statement: Images: Nikon D5600, 6000 by 4000 pixels; Nikon 200 mm F4 lens, camera at 4 m; two Bresser LG 900 54W LED panels; white-paper background.

F09.statement: Image tessellation and tracking yield square positions; the reported detection accuracy is 0.02 pixel (1 micrometre). This is a reported tracking result, not a guaranteed robot or world-coordinate accuracy.

F10.statement: Loading and unloading differ; authors attribute this to friction, viscoelasticity and self-adhesion. Experimental and simulated curves must remain separate.

F11.locator: Methods Finite-element simulation protocol, p7; Fig2
F11.statement: FEM uses Abaqus/Standard, neo-Hookean material, plane strain and CPE6H hybrid quadratic triangles, at least two elements through the narrowest features. Unit-cell periodic low-strain tests and full-structure nonlinear static tests are distinct.

F12.statement: Simulation material values are shear modulus 0.333 MPa*m and bulk modulus 16.7 GPa*m. Unit cell: a=12 mm, pretwist=0.39, hinge=0.1 mm. These are not the printed specimen dimensions or its measured physical moduli.

F13.locator: Methods Finite-element simulation protocol, p7; Fig2
F13.statement: Numerical full-structure loading includes dipole, bending and pure shear; small-strain hinge sweep in mm: 0.02,0.033,0.055,0.092,0.155,0.258,0.431,0.719,1.199,2.0. Main Results identifies a 16 by 16 unit-cell lattice.

F14.locator: Main Eqs11,15 and Methods; SI Notes1-2
F14.statement: Coarse quantities are derived from tracked neighboring square centers and C=F-transpose F. Local area-change d and nonlinear shear measure s² are distinct from linear dilation alpha. The fit error is squared displacement residual normalized by total squared observed displacement, not a pointwise tolerance.

F15.statement: Conformal fitting uses a truncated complex polynomial; source discusses approximately 20 coefficients, keeping model order well below point count and centering/rescaling positions for numerical conditioning.

F16.statement: Hinge/coarse-grained theory assumes small hinges and comparatively small nonmechanistic deformations. It excludes the near-untwisted endpoint where neglected corrections may diverge. Symmetry-derived energy is not universal for every lattice.

F17.statement: Stress derivation, perturbative linear prediction and Lagrange-multiplier theory are analytical branches. The source contains formula inconsistencies recorded separately; none is a physical stress-measurement procedure.

F18.locator: Methods boundary inference; SI Note9, pp13-14
F18.statement: Boundary inference requires a densely sampled closed boundary of a simply connected coarse domain, positive local linear dilation, model order well below half the boundary-point count, and a convention for undetermined global rotation and translation.

F19.statement: The ideal rotating-square interval 1/sqrt(2)<alpha<1 is expressed relative to a fully dilated reference. It is not an immediate stop interval for a pretwisted physical sample or a certified strength limit.

F20.statement: Experiment uses the full rectangular boundary for inference, while a gerrymandered interior boundary is used on FEM data. A nearest conformal fit and a boundary-only prediction are different analyses.

F21.statement: Boundary actuation is a spring-network simulation with six Hookean springs representing each square and boundary springs of stiffness 10^4 times the interior stiffness; it uses numerical minimization and reports qualitative agreement.

F22.locator: Discussion and Results boundary control, p6
F22.statement: Remotely actuated struts are proposed future work. The paper does not demonstrate a physical boundary-actuated device, physical kagome apparatus, or robotic implementation.

F23.statement: Data and code are cited at 10.5281/zenodo.4646672. The inspected record is v1, published 30 March 2021, links the preprint, lists two raw-image archives and processing/numerical/Mathematica archives, and reports about 30.4 GB total. Archive contents and final-figure correspondence were not inspected.

F24.statement: Movie 1 is a timelapse of foot loading; Movie 2 is a timelapse of bridge loading; Movie 3 is an animation of force-balance simulations with boundary actuation.

F25.locator: Main p9; publisher rights; Zenodo record
F25.statement: Article and listed dataset record state CC BY 4.0. Third-party credit exceptions remain relevant; the review exports only original commentary, factual records and authored requirements.

F26.statement: Physical boundary-inference residuals are much larger than the best numerical curves during portions of loading; the text claim of greater-than-99-percent capture must not become a universal physical acceptance threshold.

F27.locator: metadata and five sampled frames per video
F27.statement: Movies 1 and 2 are 400-frame physical timelapses encoded at 30 fps, about 13.33 s playback. Movie 3 is a 534-frame simulation animation at 10 fps. Playback duration is not physical loading duration; Methods specifies 1 frame/s acquisition.

F28.locator: Main Methods FEM p7; SI Note7 p11
F28.statement: Periodic unit-cell calibration strain is 5×10^-6. Source reports (K,G1,G2) approximately (35,5.2×10^4,2×10^4) Pa*m. SI gives gradient modulus K-tilde=125 Pa*m^3 at reference hinge l0=0.1 mm. Preserve these reported two-dimensional units and numerical-only scope; they are not specimen force-test calibration.

facts.statement: Czajkowski, Coulais, van Hecke and Rocklin; Nature Communications 13, 211; published 11 January 2022; DOI suffix contains 2021 but publication year is 2022.
Printed meta-beam: 306 mm length, 64 mm width, 40 mm height; 48 by 10 squares; square side 4.8 mm; hinge thickness 0.2 mm.
Connex 500 Stratasys fabrication using proprietary Agilus 30, nominal 30 Shore A; Vero Black square pads of 3.6 mm were printed on one edge for imaging.
The material is viscoelastic. Referenced short/long-time Young moduli are 3.3 MPa and 0.6 MPa; these are cited values rather than a new specimen calibration trace supplied here.

Physical branch 1 uses a foot-shaped ABS indenter printed on a Stratasys Dimension printer. Fine powder lubricates contact with the bottom surface and foot; powder identity and amount are not specified.
Foot branch: a compression-decompression cycle at 0.1 mm/s to maximum 20 mm stroke, recording 400 frames at 1 frame/s.
Physical branch 2 is a three-point bridge loading test using an Instron 5943; a compression-decompression cycle at 0.2 mm/s to maximum 40 mm stroke, recording 400 frames at 1 frame/s.
Images: Nikon D5600, 6000 by 4000 pixels; Nikon 200 mm F4 lens, camera at 4 m; two Bresser LG 900 54W LED panels; white-paper background.

Image tessellation and tracking yield square positions; the reported detection accuracy is 0.02 pixel (1 micrometre). This is a reported tracking result, not a guaranteed robot or world-coordinate accuracy.
Loading and unloading differ; authors attribute this to friction, viscoelasticity and self-adhesion. Experimental and simulated curves must remain separate.

facts.locator: Methods Finite-element simulation protocol, p7; Fig2
facts.statement: FEM uses Abaqus/Standard, neo-Hookean material, plane strain and CPE6H hybrid quadratic triangles, at least two elements through the narrowest features. Unit-cell periodic low-strain tests and full-structure nonlinear static tests are distinct.

Simulation material values are shear modulus 0.333 MPa*m and bulk modulus 16.7 GPa*m. Unit cell: a=12 mm, pretwist=0.39, hinge=0.1 mm. These are not the printed specimen dimensions or its measured physical moduli.

facts.locator: Methods Finite-element simulation protocol, p7; Fig2
facts.statement: Numerical full-structure loading includes dipole, bending and pure shear; small-strain hinge sweep in mm: 0.02,0.033,0.055,0.092,0.155,0.258,0.431,0.719,1.199,2.0. Main Results identifies a 16 by 16 unit-cell lattice.

facts.locator: Main Eqs11,15 and Methods; SI Notes1-2
facts.statement: Coarse quantities are derived from tracked neighboring square centers and C=F-transpose F. Local area-change d and nonlinear shear measure s² are distinct from linear dilation alpha. The fit error is squared displacement residual normalized by total squared observed displacement, not a pointwise tolerance.

Conformal fitting uses a truncated complex polynomial; source discusses approximately 20 coefficients, keeping model order well below point count and centering/rescaling positions for numerical conditioning.

Hinge/coarse-grained theory assumes small hinges and comparatively small nonmechanistic deformations. It excludes the near-untwisted endpoint where neglected corrections may diverge. Symmetry-derived energy is not universal for every lattice.

Stress derivation, perturbative linear prediction and Lagrange-multiplier theory are analytical branches. The source contains formula inconsistencies recorded separately; none is a physical stress-measurement procedure.

facts.locator: Methods boundary inference; SI Note9, pp13-14
facts.statement: Boundary inference requires a densely sampled closed boundary of a simply connected coarse domain, positive local linear dilation, model order well below half the boundary-point count, and a convention for undetermined global rotation and translation.

The ideal rotating-square interval 1/sqrt(2)<alpha<1 is expressed relative to a fully dilated reference. It is not an immediate stop interval for a pretwisted physical sample or a certified strength limit.

Experiment uses the full rectangular boundary for inference, while a gerrymandered interior boundary is used on FEM data. A nearest conformal fit and a boundary-only prediction are different analyses.

Boundary actuation is a spring-network simulation with six Hookean springs representing each square and boundary springs of stiffness 10^4 times the interior stiffness; it uses numerical minimization and reports qualitative agreement.

facts.locator: Discussion and Results boundary control, p6
facts.statement: Remotely actuated struts are proposed future work. The paper does not demonstrate a physical boundary-actuated device, physical kagome apparatus, or robotic implementation.

Data and code are cited at 10.5281/zenodo.4646672. The inspected record is v1, published 30 March 2021, links the preprint, lists two raw-image archives and processing/numerical/Mathematica archives, and reports about 30.4 GB total. Archive contents and final-figure correspondence were not inspected.
Movie 1 is a timelapse of foot loading; Movie 2 is a timelapse of bridge loading; Movie 3 is an animation of force-balance simulations with boundary actuation.

facts.locator: Main p9; publisher rights; Zenodo record
facts.statement: Article and listed dataset record state CC BY 4.0. Third-party credit exceptions remain relevant; the review exports only original commentary, factual records and authored requirements.

Physical boundary-inference residuals are much larger than the best numerical curves during portions of loading; the text claim of greater-than-99-percent capture must not become a universal physical acceptance threshold.

facts.locator: metadata and five sampled frames per video
facts.statement: Movies 1 and 2 are 400-frame physical timelapses encoded at 30 fps, about 13.33 s playback. Movie 3 is a 534-frame simulation animation at 10 fps. Playback duration is not physical loading duration; Methods specifies 1 frame/s acquisition.
